Each instance writes the RuntimeImpl of emitter.hpp 150-166 (em_ +0x0, explicit_args_ +0x8, remaining_base_gas_ +0x20, spill_avx_ +0x28, runtime_fun_ +0x30, arg_count_ +0x38, context_arg_ +0x40/+0x48, result_arg_ +0x50/+0x58, remaining_gas_arg_ +0x60/+0x68) and calls call_runtime_impl 0x3837e0. The code that pops operands, spills registers and places arguments is call_runtime_impl, RuntimeImpl::call_impl 0x37ede0 and mov_arg 0x36a050, which cycle 32 already ran for the division calls and which this cycle ran at all 92 sites.

cleared.check: Whether the inlined storage, hashing and log emitters of Monad's native compiler matter on the other 20 networks.
cleared.result: They do not. The emitter read here is part of the Monad validator package (monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb) and runs only on Monad. The other networks' clients and what was tested on them are listed in research/network-risk/OPCODES.md; this unit adds nothing for them.

leads.question: Wire CALLER, MSTORE and CALLDATALOAD into the whole-block runner and run block 0xde6 (clear's KECCAK256 and delta TLOAD, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:11-20 via src/PoolManager.sol:311) whole from the package on 20,000 sets with the transient store preloaded.
leads.why: Its sites matched one by one, but it is the one block with a delta read that has not run whole, and it decides how much clear() lets an account forgive.

leadResults.answer: The KECCAK256, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and LOG arms of compile_basic_blocks<MonadTraits<10>> only pass the runtime function, the remaining gas and spill_avx to out-of-line call_runtime<Args...> instances whose RuntimeImpl constants match each runtime signature. Run from the package on the logged states of all 92 sites, the streams equal the clang listing, the post-call stacks equal the hook, and 184000 runs with a reference runtime that clobbers every caller-saved register gave no wrong key, value, result or clobbered word; 80,000 whole-block runs of the lock and reserves blocks matched pyevm.py, and every planted fault was caught.

The extended hook logs gpq256_regs_ and touched_memory_size_ without changing the listing. The five touched sizes read from the listing equal the logged ones; the listing-derived limb tables differ from the logged ones only in rows the streams do not use, and term.py, block.py, task3.py, realarith.py and inl.py rerun on the logged values with every stream equal and no bad run.
